messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're kicking off a preview of ephemeral CI runners on AWS Fargate with OIDC (tokenless) auth. would like 3-5 squads to try the canary flow this week. details below.

jonathan: Nice. what's the canary scope? single repo or org-level?

maria: start with 4 repos: infra/infra-templates, devex/ci-templates, web-app/frontend, data/etl. org-wide rollouts need a follow-up plan.

rahul: What about secrets? we still need to mount KMS-encrypted envs for deploy jobs.

maria: we use short-lived session creds from our OIDC role + ssm:GetParameter for runtime secrets. no long-lived PATs in the runners. see snippet: 
```
runners:
  executor: fargate
  cert_auth: oidc
  role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-fargate-ephemeral
```

anna: Will the new runners show up in SRE tracing and logs? need to update dashboards before we flip traffic.

jonathan: yes — they emit the same opentelemetry spans. need to wire the task-id to our tracer. i'll add a hook.

sam: cost question — Fargate for short jobs is fine, but long parallel jobs could blow the budget. is there an autoscale/cap cap?

maria: autoscaler defaults: max 30 tasks per cluster for preview. cost projection for current CI volume: +5-7% at peak. we'll monitor and adjust.

rahul: fallback plan if Fargate hits capacity?

maria: fallback routes to our existing self-hosted runner pool (label: legacy). traffic policy lives in devex/ci-routing. no job will be dropped.

anna: I'll update the runbook and incident playbook to include task drain + task-arn mapping.

jonathan: can we gate by feature flag per repo? we should avoid accidental mass cutovers.

maria: yes — using repo-level runner labels. only repos on the canary list will pick ephemeral runners.

sam: i'll volunteer web-app/frontend and run a full pipeline tomorrow morning. ping me with the repo label.

maria: thanks! label is `fargate-canary`. add to repo settings and kickoff.

ci-bot: build #4023 (web-app/frontend) succeeded on ephemeral-runner-7f3d :white_check_mark:

rahul: saw the success. logs look clean. just one warning about file descriptors in the test container.

maria: noted — i'll file an issue in devex/ci-ops with the log excerpt.

jonathan: housekeeping: please avoid enabling for infra/critical until we confirm caching behaves as expected (warm caches matter).

maria: agreed. infra/critical is excluded from canary for now.

anna: timeline for moving to beta?

maria: plan: preview this week, beta in 2 weeks if no major issues, full rollout in 6 weeks. will post a summary after 3 days of canary metrics. :thumbsup:

sam: 👍

jonathan: thanks — will monitor metrics and post any anomalies in #eng-sre.

maria: thanks everyone. please DM me if you want early access or help adding the label.
